sources.title: Abbe Museum: A Meeting of Nations exhibit catalogue
sources.note: Museum synthesis of Wabanaki nations, seasonal lifeways, kin groups, trade, consensus, early voyages, and the later formal Confederacy.

sources.title: Wolastoqey Nation in New Brunswick: Our History
sources.note: Nation-authored account of Wolastoqey history, Wabanaki relationships, technologies, and seventeenth-century Confederacy formalization.

sources.title: Mi'kmaq Nation in Maine: Introduction
sources.note: Nation introduction to Mi'kmaq homelands, related distinct nations, and the Dawnland name.

sources.title: Passamaquoddy Tribe at Indian Township: Cultural Resources
sources.note: Tribal cultural-resources mission centering Passamaquoddy continuity and membership in the later Confederacy.

sources.title: Penobscot Nation: Women in Penobscot History
sources.note: Nation account of women, mothers, grandmothers, teaching, oral tradition, and counsel.

sources.title: Penobscot Nation curriculum portal
sources.note: Tribal curriculum resources on family ties, homeland, oral tradition, arts, and community relationships.

sources.title: Penobscot Nation language resources
sources.note: Living Penobscot language and modern orthography resources, used as continuity rather than an old text sample.

sources.title: Maine Department of Education: Wabanaki Studies Framework
sources.note: Current teaching framework for nation names, responsible terminology, and the 1497 to 1680s early-contact horizon.

sources.title: National Park Service: Wabanaki Life Thousands of Years Ago
sources.note: Archaeological account of seasonal canoe travel, camps, wigwams, middens, ceramics, tools, and foods at Mount Desert Island.

sources.title: National Park Service: Asticou's Island Domain, volume 1
sources.note: Regional study of Wabanaki coast history, oral tradition, seafaring, leadership, and carefully separated European voyages.

sources.title: National Park Service: Asticou's Island Domain, volume 2
sources.note: Regional inventory of material culture, plant and animal foods, medicines, sites, and later ethnographic evidence.

sources.title: Maine Historic Preservation Commission: Maine Prehistoric Archaeological Sites
sources.note: Ceramic Period chronology, water-oriented sites, pottery, settlement, household production, exchange, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Government of New Brunswick: Wolastoqiyik Ajemseg, volume 2
sources.note: Archaeological report on long occupation, Ceramic sequences, and material contexts at Ajemseg in Wolastoqey country.

sources.title: Parks Canada: The Mi'gmaq and their ancestors, Forillon's first inhabitants
sources.note: Evidence for Indigenous presence from about 1000 to 1534, fish cooking, domestic activity, lithic work, and portage.

sources.title: Hrynick and Betts: Late Maritime Woodland hunter-fisher-gatherer complexity
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of settlement, storage, aggregation, territoriality, architecture, exchange, and social complexity.

sources.title: Hrynick and Betts: Architecture and gendered space at Port Joli Harbour
sources.note: Study of dwelling floors, family occupation, gendered space, wigwams, sweathouses, and interpretive method.

sources.title: Hrynick and Betts: A Maritime Woodland period sweathouse
sources.note: Peer-reviewed identification of a possible earlier sweathouse and careful review of therapeutic and ritual interpretations.

sources.title: Hrynick and colleagues: Change and continuity at the Devil's Head Site
sources.note: Comparison of Late Maritime Woodland and protohistoric components on the St. Croix River.

sources.title: David Sanger: The Carson Site and the Late Ceramic Period in Passamaquoddy Bay
sources.note: Study of a Passamaquoddy Bay shell midden, housepit, pottery, food, seasonality, and settlement.

sources.title: W. Jesse Webb: A late Maritime Woodland Peskotomuhkati fishery
sources.note: Detailed analysis of fish remains, especially tomcod, and seasonality at one ancestral Peskotomuhkati site.

sources.title: Penobscot Nation and EPA: Wabanaki Traditional Cultural Lifeways Exposure Scenario
sources.note: Tribally reviewed modern model of traditional food, work, medicine, water, processing, and seasonal activity categories.

sources.title: Prince Edward Island: Aboriginal Cultural Connections
sources.note: Government synthesis of Mi'kmaq seasonal life, family, councils, children, education, food, and medicinal knowledge.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Museum: Aboriginal History in Nova Scotia, Mi'kmaq
sources.note: Museum account of wikuom construction, smoke openings, hide clothing, tanning, bone awls, and sinew.

sources.title: Prince Edward Island: First residents and the Arrival of the Europeans
sources.note: Account of Mi'kmaq continuity in Epekwitk and seven political districts under the Grand Council.

sources.title: Abbe Museum: Passamaquoddy Kit teacher guide
sources.note: Museum reconstruction of family, nearby kin, learning by observation and work, spatial etiquette, games, and teasing.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Traditional Mi'kmaw birchbark canoes
sources.note: Living knowledge of ocean and inland canoe designs, materials, construction, sealing, and paddles.

sources.title: Parks Canada: The Mi'gmaq and Kouchibouguac
sources.note: Mi'gma'ki archaeology and local seasonal use of marine and inland resources.

sources.title: Hudson Museum: Wabanaki virtual-tour transcript
sources.note: Museum explanations of bark shelters, containers, canoes, wigwam framing, lashings, smoke openings, and baskets.

sources.title: Hudson Museum: Barry Dana on birchbark traditions
sources.note: Contemporary Penobscot practitioner on bark, roots, cedar, containers, canoes, and hands-on teaching.

sources.title: Hudson Museum: Wabanaki vocabulary
sources.note: English museum glossary describing useful properties of birchbark and pine pitch.

sources.title: Peskotomuhkati-Wolastoqey Language Portal
sources.note: Living collaborative dictionary and video archive documenting a distinct language and its speakers.

sources.title: Abbe Museum collections
sources.note: Museum stewardship of more than twelve millennia of Wabanaki archaeological and material heritage.

sources.title: Matthew R. Bahar: A New Dawn on an Old Sea, 1500 to 1600
sources.note: History framing sixteenth-century voyagers as newcomers to an established Wabanaki maritime world.

sources.title: Newfoundland and Labrador Heritage: Evidence for a Northern Landfall
sources.note: Review of the lost Cabot log, secondhand reports, and uncertainty over the 1497 landfall.

sources.title: John L. Allen: From Cabot to Cartier
sources.note: Scholarly geographic history of exploration around Labrador and Newfoundland beginning in 1497.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Kejimkujik petroglyphs
sources.note: Mi'kmaw cultural landscape with more than five hundred sacred, vulnerable, and broadly dated petroglyphs.

sources.title: Pierre Deleage: Mi'kmaw logographic writing, 1677 to 1912
sources.note: Study dating the documented French-missionary Mi'kmaw logographic system to 1677 and later.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Museum: Mi'kmaq Portraits, pre-contact imagery
sources.note: Museum catalogue context for a pre-contact petroglyph motif, treated as visual art rather than deciphered text.

sources.title: Smithsonian Institution: Still They Remember Me, Penobscot Transformer Tales
sources.note: Catalogue description of instructive and entertaining Penobscot oral narratives recorded much later.

sources.title: Nulhegan Abenaki Band: Traditions, Toys and Games
sources.note: Abenaki account of snow snakes, birchbark toys, dice, materials, play, and skill.

proposedOverrides.name: Wabanaki (Dawnland peoples)
proposedOverrides.summary: A Dawnland regional umbrella for related, distinct Wabanaki peoples; older networks preceded the formal seventeenth-century Confederacy.
